He'll now have a chance to make an impression with the Browns in the hope of eventually being summoned for his first regular-season NFL action. Cleveland currently has a healthy wideout corps, so Guillory isn't likely to be elevated for Sunday's matchup against the Saints.

items.headline: The Browns signed Haskins to their practice squad Wednesday.
items.summary: Haskins spent the majority of the 2026 season on New England's practice squad before being cut on Oct. 17. Last season with the Chargers, the 26-year-old recorded 17 rushing attempts for 47 yards, averaging 2.8 yards per carry. He also had four receptions for 13 yards.

items.headline: Goodson rushed 12 times for 77 yards and failed to bring in his only target in the Cowboys' 27-23 win over the Colts on Sunday.
items.summary: Facing the team for which he played two-plus seasons from 2023-25, Goodson put together a highly efficient performance as a complementary option to Javonte Williams, even after leaving the game for a spell to be checked out for a knee issue. Goodson's carry and yardage totals were both season highs, as was his average of 6.4 yards per carry. The Iowa product is seeing steady usage in a run-heavy Cowboys offense, and he's logged 29 rush attempts over the last three games heading into a Week 10 home matchup against the 49ers.

items.headline: The Cowboys elevated Hudson from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday, Patrik Walker of the Cowboys' official site reports.
items.summary: Hudson will make his NFL debut if he gets into Sunday's game against the Colts. The SMU product latched on with the Cowboys as an undrafted free agent in May. Hudson is unlikely to see much action versus Indianapolis, and whether he logs any offensive snaps at all could depend upon whether fellow wideout George Pickens (questionable, hamstring) is able to play.

items.headline: Mingo (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's matchup against the Colts, Patrik Walker of the Cowboys' official site reports.
items.summary: Mingo was hurt in the second half and may not be able to return to the game. Prior to his exit, he caught one of three targets for 23 yards. With George Pickens (hamstring) and KaVontae Turpin (ribs) inactive Sunday, the Cowboys will be down to CeeDee Lamb, Ryan Flournoy, Camden Brown and Jordan Hudson at wideout if Mingo can't return.

items.headline: The Cowboys elevated Mitchell from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday, Patrik Walker of the Cowboys' official site reports.
items.summary: Mitchell was elevated for the second straight week ahead of Sunday's matchup against Indianapolis. In his 2026 debut last Sunday versus Arizona, the tight end logged a healthy 31 offensive snaps but didn't log a target or touch. How much Mitchell plays in Indianapolis will likely depend on whether Jake Ferguson (ankle) and Luke Schoonmaker (groin) are able to suit up.

items.headline: Schoonmaker (groin) is inactive for Sunday's clash against the Colts.
items.summary: Schoonmaker continues to tend to a groin issue and will miss his second straight game. He did manage a trio of limited practices during the week, so the tight end may be able to play next Sunday, Nov. 15, against San Francisco. Dallas' tight-end corps will consist of Jake Ferguson, Brevyn Spann-Ford and James Mitchell in Week 9.

items.headline: Spann-Ford caught four of five targets for 31 yards during Sunday's 33-30 overtime loss versus the Cardinals.
items.summary: Starting tight end Jake Ferguson logged only four offensive snaps before leaving Sunday's contest with an ankle injury, and Spann-Ford ended up playing a career-high 65 offensive snaps as a result. He ended up second on the team in targets behind CeeDee Lamb (11), and he could be worth a look as a streaming option in deeper formats if Ferguson is unable to suit up in Week 9 at Indianapolis.

items.headline: Turpin (ribs) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Colts, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
items.summary: Turpin has not practiced since sustaining a rib injury in Week 6 and will now miss a third consecutive contest due to the issue. The main kick and punt returner for the Cowboys has been replaced by a combination of Tyler Goodson and Jonathan Mingo, who will continue to fulfill the role in his absence.

items.headline: The Cowboys signed Corbin to their practice squad Wednesday, Joe Hoyt of The Dallas Morning News reports.
items.summary: Corbin was released from Dallas' active roster on Tuesday but is now set to join the team's practice squad. The 26-year-old didn't see any action across the first seven weeks of the campaign and hasn't appeared in a regular-season game since 2023 with the Giants.

items.headline: Adkins caught both of his targets for four yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 28-24 win over the Chiefs.
items.summary: The block-first tight end secured a two-yard score in the fourth quarter to pull the Broncos within three points, before they scored the eventual game-winning touchdown on the next possession. Adkins now has six grabs for 44 yards and a score on seven targets this season. He has no fantasy appeal.

items.headline: Dobbins rushed four times for 18 yards and caught his only target for four yards during Sunday's 26-21 win over Carolina.
items.summary: Dobbins saw 13 fewer carries than rookie running back Jonah Coleman (17-57-1) in the game. The four rushes were a season low for Dobbins, and he figures to continue to operate as the team's No. 2 option in the backfield moving forward.

items.headline: Ehlinger (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against Carolina but is listed as the team's emergency quarterback, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Ehlinger is officially inactive Sunday, though he will be available if Bo Nix and Jarrett Stidham exit the contest due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Engram failed to catch any of his three targets in Sunday's 28-24 win over the Chiefs.
items.summary: Bo Nix targeted 10 different pass catchers on 32 total pass attempts, and it was rookie RB Jonah Coleman who led the team in receiving with a 4-63-0 line on five targets. Engram has just three catches for 15 yards over his last three games and isn't a recommended fantasy bet ahead of Sunday's date with the Panthers.

items.headline: Franklin failed to bring in either of his two targets in the Broncos' 30-16 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
items.summary: Franklin played 28 offensive snaps in Sunday's contest. Despite being on the field for 46 percent of the Broncos' offensive plays, the No. 3 option was targeted only twice and failed to catch either pass.

items.headline: Humphrey (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game versus the Panthers, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Humphrey has appeared in Denver's last four regular-season contests. However, he will be a healthy scratch for the meeting with Carolina, meaning his next opportunity to play will come in Week 11 against the Raiders, following the Broncos' bye.

items.headline: Mims (ankle) practiced fully Thursday,Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.
items.summary: Mims was a limited participant in Wednesday's session, but the wideout's full participation a day later sets the stage for him to be available Sunday against the Chiefs. The 2023 second-rounder has two catches in each of his last three games, with his Week 8 fantasy upside linked to the status of top WR Jaylen Waddle, who is managing a chest injury.

items.headline: The Broncos elevated Schrader from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday ahead of Sunday's matchup in Carolina, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Schrader has been elevated for the second straight week after making his Broncos debut last Sunday against Kansas City. He logged just two offensive snaps and didn't get a touch or target in that game, but he he did rack up 50 yards on two kick returns. Schrader figures to fill a similar role against the Panthers as the No. 3 RB behind Jonah Coleman and J.K. Dobbins.

items.headline: The Broncos placed Harvey (knee) on injured reserve Saturday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
items.summary: Harvey was already ruled out for Sunday's contest against the Chiefs, but now that he's on IR, the second-year running back will be required to miss at least the next four games. That means the earliest that he is eligible to return is Week 13 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Dec. 6. In Harvey's absence, the Broncos' backfield will be led by J.K. Dobbins and rookie fourth-rounder Jonah Coleman.

items.headline: Patterson was signed to the Broncos' practice squad Tuesday, Aric DiLalla of the team's official website reports.
items.summary: Patterson was cut from the Browns' practice squad Oct. 27, but he has now found another opportunity with Denver. With RJ Harvey (knee) on injured reserve for at least three more games, Patterson will provide the Broncos with another option in the backfield behind Jonah Coleman and J.K. Dobbins.

items.headline: LaPorta brought in four of five targets for 32 yards in the Lions' 19-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
items.summary: LaPorta finished a distant second in receptions, receiving yards and targets on a quiet day for the Lions' passing attack. The fourth-year tight end had back-to-back 80-plus-yard efforts in Weeks 4 and 5, but he's totaled a modest 83 total receiving yards over the subsequent three contests. LaPorta will look to boost his production back up in the Week 10 matchup against the Patriots in Germany next Sunday.

items.headline: Saylors (neck) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
items.summary: Saylors carried a questionable designation heading into this contest, though he won't be on the field in Week 9, marking his first absence of the 2026 campaign. With Sione Vaki (ankle) available, Saylors likely wouldn't have been very involved, regardless.

items.headline: The Lions elevated Small from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday ahead of Sunday's matchup versus the Dolphins.
items.summary: Small signed with the team's practice squad in September and is now set to be elevated for the first time this season. With Sione Vaki (ankle) and Jacob Saylors (neck) both dealing with injuries, Small could be in line to serve as Detroit's No. 2 running back behind Jahmyr Gibbs against Miami.

items.headline: St. Brown brought in eight of 10 targets for 86 yards in the Lions' 19-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
items.summary: St. Brown set the pace across the board for the Lions in receptions, receiving yards and targets. St. Brown was playing through a rib issue that had limited him throughout the practice week, but he turned in an efficient effort that included his fifth straight game with six or more catches. St. Brown's touchdown drought did extend to five games, and he'll once again aim to snap it in next Sunday's Week 10 matchup against the Patriots in Germany.

items.headline: TeSlaa caught one of his two targets for 10 yards in the Lions' 20-17 win over the Packers on Sunday.
items.summary: TeSlaa played 33 offensive snaps for the Lions in the contest, a 49 percent share of Detroit's offensive plays. However, TeSlaa saw a mere two targets for the second straight game after logging a season-high eight against the Panthers in Week 4, and Sunday's catch was his first since that game as well.

items.headline: Vaki (ankle) is available for Sunday's game against Miami.
items.summary: Vaki didn't practice Friday, resulting in a questionable tag for Week 9. However, he will be out there against the Dolphins and may continue to be more involved after totaling 11 carries in the Week 8 win over the Vikings.

items.headline: Williams brought in one of two targets for 31 yards and rushed once for nine yards in the Lions' 19-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
items.summary: Williams and the rest of the Lions' air attack had a quiet afternoon, as Jared Goff threw for just 170 yards overall. Williams was efficient on his two touches, but he finished with a new season low in receiving yards. The 2022 first-round pick, who's averaging 16.7 yards per reception on the season, will likely be busier in a Week 10 matchup against the Patriots in Germany next Sunday.

items.headline: Lions coach Dan Campbell said Friday that Pacheco (back) has a chance to return in late December, Justin Rogers of DetroitFootball.net reports.
items.summary: Pacheco has been sidelined for the entirety of the regular season to this point after undergoing back surgery in September. Sione Vaki has been working as the Lions' clear RB2, though Jahmyr Gibbs has been a true workhorse out of the backfield. If Pacheco does return at the end of the regular season, it's hard to envision him having a big impact coming off back surgery.

items.headline: The Packers elevated Dabney from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
items.summary: Dabney is set to suit up for his first contest of the 2026 regular season. With Josh Whyle (concussion) ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Patriots, Dabney will be the No. 4 tight end behind Tucker Kraft, Mark Redman and Jonnu Smith.

items.headline: Kraft brought in one of three targets for one yard and rushed twice for eight yards in the Packers' 45-27 win over the Patriots on Sunday.
items.summary: The athletic tight end didn't get in on any of the fun on a day when Jordan Love threw for 372 yards and three touchdowns. Kraft's stat line set (receptions, receiving yards) or tied (targets) season lows, while his work on the ground included a pair of season-high figures. Nevertheless, it was an utterly forgettable showing for Kraft, who'll look to atone in a Week 10 home divisional clash against the Vikings next Sunday.

items.headline: Lloyd (knee) is listed as inactive Sunday at New England, Mike Spofford of the Packers' official site reports.
items.summary: The Packers added Lloyd to the Week 9 injury report Thursday as limited due to a knee injury, and he maintained that activity level Friday before the team tagged him as questionable ahead of the weekend. Now that Lloyd is confirmed to be unavailable, Pierre Strong and Kaleb Johnson will be the team's complementary backfield options behind No. 1 option Josh Jacobs.

items.headline: Melton exited Sunday's game against the Patriots and is being evaluated for a concussion.
items.summary: Melton wasn't targeted prior to departing, but he did return four kicks for 110 yards. J. Michael Sturdivant will be next up for wideout snaps behind Matthew Golden, Christian Watson and Savion Williams.

items.headline: Smith (coach's decision) is inactive for Thursday's game against the Panthers Mike Spofford of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Smith has appeared in each of the Packers' seven regular-season games. However, he will be a healthy scratch Thursday night, meaning Mark Redman and Josh Whyle will be behind Tucker Kraft on the depth chart.

items.headline: Whyle (concussion) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Patriots, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
items.summary: Whyle was unable to clear the NFL's five-step concussion protocol ahead of Sunday's contest. The No. 3 tight end will be replaced by Jonnu Smith for the showdown with the Patriots.

items.headline: The Packers didn't activate Brooks (ankle) from injured reserve Saturday, Weston Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
items.summary: Brooks landed on IR in early October and has missed the required four games. He was designated to return Wednesday and was limited in practice all week before drawing a tag of questionable for Sunday's game against New England. The running back didn't end up being activated Saturday, so Brooks isn't eligible to suit up again until at least Sunday, Nov. 15, against Minnesota.

items.headline: The Packers signed Miller to the practice squad Monday, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: By all accounts, both Jordan Love and Tyrod Taylor are healthy on the 53-man roster, so the signing seems to strictly be for organizational-depth purposes. Miller joins Kedon Slovis as quarterbacks currently on the team's practice squad.

items.headline: Harrison caught two of three targets for 20 yards during Sunday's 44-22 win over the Chargers.
items.summary: Harrison ranked seventh on the team in targets, and although C.J. Stroud connected with four different wide receivers for five total touchdowns, Harrison was not one of them. Harrison has now reeled in six of 11 targets for 60 yards and a score over three contests with the Texans, and he will remain hard to trust from a fantasy perspective in Week 10 versus Cleveland.

items.headline: Marks turned 18 carries into 70 yards and hauled in one of four targets for four yards during Sunday's 44-22 road win over the Chargers.
items.summary: Marks acted as the Texans' primary running back for a fourth straight game, three of which David Montgomery has missed completely due to a groin injury. During that stretch, Marks has racked up 75 touches for 321 yards from scrimmage, but he has yet to reach the end zone since Week 4. Montgomery wasn't able to practice this week, so Marks may be in line for another role as Houston's No. 1 backfield option next Sunday at Cleveland if the former doesn't make the requisite progress in his recovery.

items.headline: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said Wednesday that Montgomery (groin) has made some progress but is still viewed as week-to-week and will remain out for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports.
items.summary: Montgomery missed Houston's last two games before a Week 8 bye, and he doesn't look like he'll be ready to return to action any sooner than Nov. 15, when the Texans face the Browns on the road. With Montgomery set to miss another game, Woody Marks is poised to maintain a lead role out of the backfield. While Montgomery was sidelined the previous two contests, Marks averaged 81.0 scrimmage yards on 18.5 touches per game.

items.headline: Moreau played 21 offensive snaps and nine special-teams snaps in the Texans' 27-21 overtime loss to the Giants on Sunday.
items.summary: Moreau did not appear in the box score of Sunday's game. The tight end's complete lack of offensive production was in stark contrast to his Week 6 two-touchdown effort against the Jaguars in London, and Moreau's week-to-week production figures to remain erratic while working behind clear No. 1 option Dalton Schultz.

items.headline: Ogunbowale didn't record an offensive touch or target in Sunday's 24-21 overtime loss to the Giants.
items.summary: Even with David Montgomery (groin) and Jawhar Jordan (quadriceps) injured and inactive, Ogunbowale played just seven offensive snaps behind Woody Marks' 54. Ogunbowale can continue to be ignored in fantasy football.

items.headline: Schultz caught two of four targets for 42 yards in Sunday's 44-22 win over the Chargers.
items.summary: Not counting his 12-140-0 receiving explosion in Week 2 when Nico Collins was out with a hamstring injury, Schultz has mustered 23 grabs for 244 yards and no touchdowns across his seven other appearances. He's failed to reach 50 receiving yards in any of those contests and is merely a TE2 in fantasy.

items.headline: The Texans signed Pitsenberger to the practice squad Monday.
items.summary: Undrafted out of Yale last spring, Pitsenberger signed with the Texans and spent the 2026 offseason with the team before suffering an ankle injury during training camp. Now healthy, he's back with the team via the practice squad. He ran nine times for 33 yards in one preseason appearance.

items.headline: The Texans signed Sobkowicz to the practice squad Wednesday.
items.summary: Sobkowicz was on Houston's practice squad for the first five weeks of the season before being cut in October. The 24-year-old has yet to make a regular-season appearance for the Texans. Landing back on the team's practice squad, the undrafted rookie has a long way to go before making his NFL debut.

items.headline: Alie-Cox is questionable to return to Sunday's game against Dallas due to a groin injury.
items.summary: Alie-Cox exited in the fourth quarter and was subsequently deemed questionable to return. The veteran tight end has been a minor part of Indianapolis' offense this season, logging four catches through eight games. Alie-Cox hadn't recorded a catch or target prior to his departure Sunday.

items.headline: Allen caught all seven targets for 67 yards in Sunday's 42-7 loss to the Jaguars.
items.summary: The veteran wideout finished second on the team in targets, three behind Tyler Warren on a day Colts QBs attempted 30 passes. When on the field this season, Allen has been a consistent target-earner who runs routes that are friendly to quarterbacks in the short areas of the field. Not a big-play threat whatsoever at this stage of his career, Allen is averaging a career-low 9.0 yards per catch on 36 grabs this season. He has just one touchdown and is a low-upside WR4 for fantasy purposes headed into next Sunday's game against the Cowboys.

items.headline: Dulin caught one of two targets for a 55-yard touchdown in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys. He added three rushing yards on one attempt.
items.summary: Dulin caught a screen pass at the line of scrimmage and raced all the way down the left sideline for the touchdown on his big play to pull the Colts within three points at the end of the third quarter. He still ran just six routes on Daniel Jones' 38 dropbacks against Dallas, leaving Dulin out of the fantasy picture unless the Colts make some trades at the position before Tuesday's deadline.

items.headline: Giddens racked up 43 yards on six carries in Indianapolis' Week 8 loss to Jacksonville on Sunday.
items.summary: Giddens entered Sunday having not logged a snap this season, but he got an opportunity in the blowout loss and made the most of it, ripping off a pair of 12-yard runs on the way to a team-leading 43 rushing yards. However, it must be noted that he didn't enter until the game was far out of reach in the fourth quarter, so all of his production came in garbage time. Still, it was a meaningful performance by Giddens in the context of Indianapolis fielding trade offers for star RB Jonathan Taylor amidst a lost season. Should Taylor indeed be dealt, Giddens would immediately take on a more prominent role in the Colts backfield along with seventh-round rookie Seth McGowan.

items.headline: Gould (concussion) does not have a designation for Sunday's matchup versus Dallas.
items.summary: Gould missed Indianapolis' previous two games while in concussion protocol. However, he was a full practice participant throughout this week and has been cleared to suit up by an independent neurologist. Gould likely will return to his usual specialist role as a kickoff and punt returner, though he probably won't be involved much in the passing game given that he's logged just one offensive snap through six games this season.

items.headline: Leonard (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Cowboys but is listed as the team's emergency quarterback, Abby Halpin of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: As has been the case throughout the season, Leonard is a healthy scratch. However, he will be available if Daniel Jones and Anthony Richardson exit the contest due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Mallory did not catch any of his three targets during Sunday's 16-10 loss to Minnesota.
items.summary: Mallory and the other Colts tight ends worked in larger roles offensively Sunday due to the absence of Tyler Warren (groin). However, the former's 21 offensive snaps ranked third behind Mo Alie-Cox (39) and Drew Ogletree (35), and Mallory could not connect with Daniel Jones, with the third and final pass that came his way resulting in an interception by Harrison Smith. Mallory has seen nine targets over his last two games since coming off injured reserve, but his role would shrink against the Jaguars in Week 8 if Warren is given the green light to play in that contest.

items.headline: Ogletree (knee) does not carry an official injury designation ahead of Sunday's game versus the Cowboys.
items.summary: Ogletree was able to play through his nagging knee issue in Week 8 at Jacksonville, and he'll be active again in Week 9 despite missing practice Wednesday and logging a limited practice session Thursday. He figures to continue to compete with Mo Alie-Cox and Will Mallory for snaps at tight end behind clear frontrunner Tyler Warren.

items.headline: Richardson entered the Colts' 42-7 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday for an ineffective Daniel Jones with 11:45 remaining and completed both his pass attempts for eight yards while rushing twice for four yards.
items.summary: As his final line indicates, Richardson did little in mop-up duty, but James Boyd of The Athletic reports that head coach Shane Steichen has pledged a top-to-bottom evaluation ahead of a Week 9 home matchup against the Cowboys next Sunday. With Indianapolis at 2-6 and both Jonathan Taylor and Josh Downs reportedly on the trade block, Steichen may ultimately conclude there's little to lose in giving Richardson, the 2023 fourth-overall pick, another run at the starting job he's struggled with previously.

items.headline: Treadwell caught one of two targets for 18 yards during Sunday's 42-7 loss to the Jaguars.
items.summary: Treadwell failed to record multiple receptions in a game for the first time since Week 3 against Houston. The wide receiver could be set to operate in a more prominent role if the team decides to deal fellow wideout Josh Downs prior to the trade deadline Nov. 10. For the time being, Treadwell doesn't figure to have much fantasy appeal Sunday against the Cowboys.

items.headline: Warren brought in four of seven targets for 44 yards in the Colts' 27-23 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday.
items.summary: Warren tied for second in receptions and finished as the runner-up in both receiving yards and targets after a slow start to Sunday's loss. The second-year tight end's role could be even bigger by next Sunday's Week 10 home matchup against the Dolphins, as the Colts could conceivably move both Josh Downs and Jonathan Taylor, not to mention quarterback Daniel Jones, by Tuesday's trade deadline. Warren has at least four receptions in every game with the exception of Week 1 heading into the aforementioned matchup against Miami.

items.headline: When asked Wednesday when Pierce (heel) might be able to return to practice, Colts head coach Shane Steichen noted that he "can't put a timetable on it right now," Kevin Bowen of 107.5 The Fan Indianapolis reports.
items.summary: Steichen said that Pierce, who has been on IR since Sept. 26, is currently rehabbing his injury, but the wideout's return is clearly not imminent. At 2-6, the Colts, who are already sellers ahead of the NFL trade deadline, have little incentive to rush Pierce back. Meanwhile, fellow WR Josh Downs has asked to be dealt, a situation that further clouds the team's pass-catching corps ahead of Week 9.

items.headline: Abdullah carried the ball seven times for 30 yards and returned one kickoff for 24 yards in Thursday night's 33-10 win over the Ravens.
items.summary: Abdullah recorded the third-most-offensive snaps in the backfield (seven), behind Chris Rodriguez (25) and Bayshul Tuten (20). Should everyone in the backfield remain healthy, Abdullah will likely see a similar workload for the rest of the season.

items.headline: Allen (hamstring) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Colts.
items.summary: Allen popped up on Thursday's injury report due to a hamstring injury, but despite logging back-to-back limited practices to end Week 8 prep, the second-year running back has been cleared to play in Sunday's AFC South tilt. He has only one carry through six regular-season games while operating as the team's RB3 behind Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez.

items.headline: Boerkircher hauled in two of three targets for 61 yards in Thursday night's 33-10 win over Baltimore.
items.summary: Boerkircher was tied with Parker Washington for the second-most receiving yards on the team with 61. This game marks the fourth time this season that the rookie has surpassed 30 snaps on offense. Boerkircher has made a name for himself as Jacksonville's No. 2 option at tight end behind Brenton Strange.

items.headline: Cameron caught his only target for six yards in Thursday night's 33-10 victory over the Ravens.
items.summary: Cameron didn't see the ball until the fourth quarter despite playing the third most snaps at wide receiver (25) for the Jaguars on Thursday, behind only Parker Washington (38) and Jakobi Meyers (38). This marks the third game in a row during which the 23-year-old played as the Jaguars' No. 3 option at receiver, but his limited usage keeps him as a low-priority waiver-wire add.

items.headline: Hunter caught his only target for minus-1 yard and lost a fumble in Thursday night's 33-10 win over the Ravens.
items.summary: Hunter played six offensive snaps against Baltimore but turned the ball over on his only touch. After posting a 4-59-1 receiving line against the Texans in London back in Week 6, Hunter has done very little on offense. He needs the Jaguars' opponents to make games closer so the coaching staff feels obligated to utilize Hunter's big-play ability.

items.headline: Koziol finished Thursday's 33-10 win over Baltimore with two catches for 15 yards on two targets.
items.summary: Koziol was part of a three-tight-end starting unit for Jacksonville alongside Brenton Strange and Nate Boerkircher. Koziol logged the fewest offensive snaps (12) among the trio but matched both in receptions. He entered Thursday with just one catch through five contests, so it's probably not wise to count on him for substantial production moving forward.

items.headline: Rodriguez rushed 10 times for 19 yards and a touchdown and brought in both targets for 13 yards in the Jaguars' 33-10 win over the Ravens on Thursday night.
items.summary: Rodriguez finished with just two fewer carries than Bhayshul Tuten, who came into the game managing ankle and foot injuries and was able to log a relatively abbreviated workload thanks to game script. Both backs had plenty of trouble against Baltimore's stout run defense, but Rodriguez salvaged his fantasy night with a two-yard TD run just past the midway point of the fourth quarter. Rodriguez now has scored in back-to-back games heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.

items.headline: Strange caught both of his targets for 22 yards in Thursday night's 33-10 win over the Ravens.
items.summary: The Jaguars keep blowing teams out and aren't being pushed on offense, which is keeping Trevor Lawrence's pass volume low. Strange is still making the most of his few opportunities, totaling four grabs for 77 yards on four targets over the last two weeks, games in which the Jaguars have combined to outscore their opponents 75-17. Strange is a TE1 for fantasy and gets a date with the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.

items.headline: How does Jessie Bates III help the Jaguars defense? Are Falcons still contending?
items.summary: The Falcons decided it was wiser to get something for Bates now rather than letting him walk in free agency.

items.headline: Allen caught two of three targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 28-24 loss to the Broncos.
items.summary: The rookie wide receiver usurped Jalen Royals on the depth chart, operating as the clear WR3 behind Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy. Allen ran 22 routes on Patrick Mahomes' 44 dropbacks, but with both Rice and Worthy healthy alongside Travis Kelce and Kenneth Walker, there doesn't appear to be much juice to squeeze for Allen.

items.headline: Armstrong caught one of two targets for three yards during Sunday night's 20-3 loss to Seattle.
items.summary: Armstrong was signed to the active roster ahead of Week 7, and he was on the field for 56 percent of the team's offensive snaps. With Rashee Rice (hamstring) still banged up, it's possible that Armstrong operates in a similar role in Week 8 versus Denver.

items.headline: Gray caught both of his targets for 15 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 28-24 loss to the Broncos.
items.summary: The Chiefs' TE2 caught a four-yard score in the third quarter, his first touchdown of the season. Kansas City uses plenty of 12 personnel, deploying both Travis Kelce and Gray on offense, but Gray handles more of the blocking duties. On the season, he has 14 grabs for 173 yards and a touchdown. There isn't much meat on the bone here for fantasy purposes.

items.headline: Kelce brought in four of six targets for 72 yards in the Chiefs' 35-12 win over the Jets on Sunday. He also rushed once for one yard.
items.summary: Kelce led the Chiefs in receiving yards and finished second in targets on the afternoon, and his tally in the former category also served as the legendary tight end's second highest of the season. Kelce got there with a big boost from a game-high 38-yard catch, and he'll take a formidable 33-482-2 line into a Week 10 road matchup against the Falcons next Sunday.

items.headline: Nussmeier is inactive for Sunday's game against the Jets but will serve as the Chiefs' emergency third quarterback.
items.summary: It's a familiar role for the rookie seventh-round pick, who has served as the emergency No. 3 QB regularly this year. Nussmeier won't be able to see the field unless both Patrick Mahomes and Justin Fields exit due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Remigio is officially active for Sunday's game against the Jets.
items.summary: The 27-year-old was questionable due to a hip issue, but it's no surprise he's suiting up after putting in full practice sessions Thursday and Friday. Remigio has played just two offensive snaps this year but has operated as Kansas City's primary return man and should continue to do so Sunday.

items.headline: Watson reverted to the Chiefs' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's official transaction log.
items.summary: Watson was elevated to the active roster for a second week in a row ahead of Sunday night's 20-3 loss to the Seahawks. The wide receiver reeled in his only target for seven yards while playing five snaps on offense and two snaps with the special-teams unit. The Chiefs can elevate Watson one more time before the team would have to officially sign him to the active roster.

items.headline: Coach Andy Reid said Monday that Worthy (hamstring) is considered day-to-day in advance of Sunday's game against the Falcons, Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' official site reports.
items.summary: The same applies to QB Patrick Mahomes (elbow), with the status of both key Kansas City skill players worth monitoring closely in the coming days. If Worthy is limited or out this weekend, added reps behind top WR Rashee Rice would be available for Cyrus Allen, Jalen Royals and Andrew Armstrong.

items.headline: The Chiefs signed De Jesus to their practice squad Wednesday.
items.summary: De Jesus joined the Chiefs as an undrafted free agent in May and was subsequently waived in August, but he is now set to rejoin the team's practice squad. The 24-year-old will now look to be elevated and make his regular-season debut.

items.headline: Means was signed to the Chiefs' practice squad Thursday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
items.summary: Means worked out with the team Wednesday, and he has now inked a deal to head join Kansas City. The wide receiver was sidelined for a couple weeks while on the practice-squad injured list with Cleveland due to a knee injury, but he now appears to be back to full health.

items.headline: Bech finished without a target or touch in Sunday's 38-33 Week 8 win over the Jets.
items.summary: Bech returned from a four-game absence due to a forearm injury and logged a 40 percent offensive snap share, but he didn't get any looks from QB Kirk Cousins. In fact, Cousins didn't go to his wideout corps as a whole very often -- 16 of his 26 targets went to tight ends, and another four went to running back Ashton Jeanty. Bech will look to get back into the box score Sunday in a Week 9 matchup in San Francisco.

items.headline: Benson (coach's decision) is a healthy scratch for Sunday's battle against San Francisco.
items.summary: It's the second straight week the rookie wideout is a healthy scratch. Benson hasn't been able to gain much traction in the offense this season, as he's notched just two catches for 12 yards on nine targets through seven games. He's also contributed as a punt returner, and Dylan Laube could assume that role in Benson's absence Sunday.

items.headline: Mayer caught all three of his targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers.
items.summary: The tight end was inches and a couple breaks away from having a much bigger afternoon, as he lost a fumble just before crossing the goal line on what would have been a 25-yard touchdown. He then had another score called back on a penalty in the second half. Mayer has alternated big games with down ones this season, and he'll try to rebound next Sunday in a tough spot against the Seahawks' strong defense.

items.headline: Nailor caught two of four targets for nine yards during Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers.
items.summary: Nailor was a non-factor on offense in Week 9, failing to reach double-digit receiving yards for the fourth time this season. The wide receiver has had a hard time getting into a groove in his first season with Las Vegas, catching 14 of 28 targets for 122 yards and a touchdown over eight contests so far.

items.headline: O'Connell (coach's decision) is inactive and serving as the Raiders' emergency third quarterback Sunday versus San Francisco.
items.summary: O'Connell has regularly been Las Vegas' emergency QB this season and has yet to log any game action. He won't be able to enter Sunday's matchup unless both Kirk Cousins and Fernando Mendoza have to exit due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Thomas (shoulder) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Jets, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Thomas was a full participant in Friday's practice, which was enough for him to fade an injury tag for Sunday's road tilt. He has five catches on as many targets for 60 yards and one touchdown through seven regular-season games and will continue to serve as the Raiders' TE3 behind Brock Bowers and Michael Mayer.

items.headline: Thornton (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the 49ers.
items.summary: Thornton recovered from a back injury Friday and entered the weekend with no injury designation. The wide receiver's inactive status, despite his health, points to some other motive from coach Klint Kubiak. Dareke Young is set to be the No. 4 wide receiver in Thornton's place.

items.headline: Tucker caught four of eight targets for 55 yards during Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers.
items.summary: Tucker finished tied for the team lead in targets with tight end Brock Bowers, garnering at least five targets for the fifth time in the team's last six contests. The wide receiver rebounded well after being blanked in Week 8 versus the Jets, securing four or more receptions for the seventh time this season. Tucker has now reeled in 33 of 56 targets for 529 yards and four touchdowns over the Raiders' first nine games during the 2026 campaign.

items.headline: White was signed by the Raiders on Thursday, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: White was released by the team Tuesday to make room for Carter Runyon (foot), who was activated off injured reserve. With Runyon now waived and potentially joining the Raiders' practice squad, White was re-signed. To date, the 27-year-old has had the best season of his career, amassing eight catches (19 targets) for 112 yards and three touchdowns.

items.headline: Las Vegas signed Runyon to its practice squad Friday, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: Runyon was not claimed by another club after the Raiders waived him from their active roster Thursday, so they were able to keep him as a member of the practice squad. Barring an injury to one of the tight ends on the 53-man roster, Runyon's path to regular-season snaps is unclear.

items.headline: Davis caught one of two targets for a 15-yard touchdown in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans.
items.summary: With Justin Herbert (finger) out of the game and the score out of hand already, Davis caught a 15-yard touchdown from backup DJ Uiagalelei in the fourth quarter. Davis has no fantasy value as a reserve wideout in one of the league's worst offenses.

items.headline: Gadsden caught all five of his targets for 52 yards during Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams.
items.summary: Gadsden was able to lead the team in catches while he finished with one fewer target than team leader Ladd McConkey. The tight end has now reeled in at least three passes for the second straight game and third time over the last four contests after having failed to do so in any of the team's first three regular-season games. Gadsden and the rest of the Chargers will face a tough test in Week 9 against the Texans.

items.headline: Harris caught all three of his targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams.
items.summary: After missing Week 6 with a hamstring injury, Harris was healthy coming out of the Week 7 bye but played pretty clearly behind both Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston against the Rams. Harris ran just 20 routes to McConkey's 34 and Johnston's 30. Harris would see a big boost if Johnston gets traded ahead of next week's deadline.

items.headline: Kolar caught one of four targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams.
items.summary: The tight end's four targets tied for third on the team, as he ran 17 routes on Justin Herbert's 37 dropbacks against Los Angeles. More of a blocker than receiver, Kolar has been forced to catch more passes out of necessity at times this season. He has 10 grabs for 98 yards on 17 targets. The catches and targets are both career highs in his fifth season.

items.headline: Lambert-Smith did not garner a target during Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams.
items.summary: Lambert-Smith was expected to revert back to a minimal role on offense in Week 8 due to both Ladd McConkey and Tre' Harris returning to action, and that is exactly what happened. Lambert-Smith played just two offensive snaps in the contest, and he will continue to have little to no fantasy value as long as the rest of the Chargers' primary pass catchers are healthy.

items.headline: Mitchell rushed seven times for 33 yards and caught three of four targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans. He also lost a fumble.
items.summary: Mitchell led LA's three-man backfield rotation with 67 scrimmage yards, while Omarion Hampton had 60 and Kimani Vidal contributed 36. Mitchell's fumble came late in the third quarter, with the Chargers already trailing 31-9 at the time. The winless Chargers are averaging a league-low 15.1 points per game heading into a Week 10 trip to Baltimore, and things could get even worse if QB Justin Herbert (finger) has to miss time after getting injured in the fourth quarter.

items.headline: Thompson (quadriceps/hamstring) is inactive against Houston on Sunday.
items.summary: This doesn't come as a surprise, as Thompson was doubtful heading into the contest after sitting out practice all week. The rookie wideout hasn't logged any game action since Week 2, and it's unclear if he'll be able to return next Monday in Baltimore. Thompson's continued absence will dent the depth of Los Angeles' wideout corps.

items.headline: Uiagalelei completed two of seven passes for 27 yards and a touchdown after replacing Justin Herbert (finger) in the fourth quarter of Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans, and head coach Jim Harbaugh said after the game that Herbert could have a fractured finger, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
items.summary: Uiagalelei was inaccurate in his first taste of regular-season NFL action but threw a 15-yard touchdown pass to Derius Davis. If Herbert isn't available to face the Ravens on MNF in Week 10 and Trey Lance (groin) isn't ready to return from injured reserve, Uiagalelei would presumably be tabbed for the first regular-season start of the latter's career.

items.headline: Vidal rushed eight times for 23 yards and caught both of his targets for seven yards in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams.
items.summary: The Chargers continue to use a fantasy-unfriendly three-man backfield, giving all three of Vidal, Omarion Hampton and Keaton Mitchell meaningful touches and snaps. In a broken Los Angeles offense and crowded group of RBs, Vidal has minimal fantasy appeal outside of deeper formats.

items.headline: Njoku (fibula) wasn't activated from IR-designated to return ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans, per the NFL's official transaction log.
items.summary: Njoku returned to practice this week but was limited all three days before being deemed doubtful for Week 9 action. The TE's next chance to play will arrive Monday, Nov. 16, when the Chargers face the Ravens.

items.headline: The Chargers signed Palmer to the practice squad Tuesday.
items.summary: Palmer spent a brief amount of time with both the Patriots and Cardinals during training camp, but he's been without a team until Tuesday. He's appeared in only one regular-season game since entering the league as a sixth-round selection of the Cardinals in the 2024 NFL Draft. The Chargers face the Rams on Sunday, and Palmer could be a candidate for elevation to the active roster depending on the statuses of fellow wide receivers Ladd McConkey (concussion), Tre' Harris (hamstring) and Brenen Thompson (quadriceps).

items.headline: Atwell wasn't targeted in Sunday's 35-21 win over the Raiders.
items.summary: With Davante Adams (hamstring) out, Atwell was active and played 25 offensive snaps. He ran 20 routes on Matthew Stafford's 32 dropbacks, tying Konata Mumpfield for second on the team behind Puka Nacua's 31, but Atwell was just doing cardio out there. He's not a reliable fantasy target, even with Adams injured.

items.headline: Higbee caught one of two targets for 14 yards against the Chargers in Sunday's 24-9 victory.
items.summary: Higbee logged a hearty 83 percent offensive snap share, most among Rams tight ends. However, he got little attention from quarterback Matthew Stafford, recording just two targets. Higbee had a nice run in Weeks 3-5, when he logged 18 catches for 212 yards across the three-game span. However, since then he's posted just seven receptions for 50 yards across his subsequent three contests. As such, it's hard to trust Higbee on a week-to-week basis right now even with the Rams down multiple pass catchers in Davante Adams (hamstring - IR), Terrance Ferguson (ankle - IR) and Colby Parkinson (ribs).

items.headline: Mumpfield caught one of two targets for 15 yards during Sunday's 35-21 win at Las Vegas.
items.summary: With Davante Adams (hamstring) on IR and Puka Nacua dealing with a calf injury going into game day, it looked like Mumpfield was going to see his role expand in Week 7. While he was second on the team in snaps (28) at wide receiver Sunday, Mumpfield still lagged far behind Nacua (58). As long as the latter remains available, Mumpfield appears unlikely to draw more than a few targets in any given game.

items.headline: Parkinson (ribs) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Commanders.
items.summary: Parkinson, who was inactive in Week 8, managed to log a limited practice Friday, before being listed as questionable for the contest. With Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) -- who was initially slated to return to action this week but subsequently ruled out -- still not in the mix, the return of Parkinson, who has caught five passes in each of the last two games he played, is a welcome boost to a Rams TE corps that also includes Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen and Max Klare.

items.headline: The Rams activated Rivers (calf) from injured reserve Saturday.
items.summary: Rivers missed six games while on injured reserve with a calf injury he sustained in the Rams' Week 2 loss to the Giants. The 27-year-old has returned ahead of Sunday's game against the Commanders and has no injury designation headed into the contest. Rivers will likely be a special-teams contributor with no real role in the Rams' offense.

items.headline: Simpson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Rams' emergency third quarterback in Sunday's game against the Commanders, Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site reports.
items.summary: Simpson will once again be inactive behind quarterbacks Matthew Stafford and Stetson Bennett. The first-round rookie will only be eligible to play if both Stafford and Bennett exit the contest due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Whittington (back) is active for Sunday's game against the Commanders.
items.summary: Whittington was a limited participant throughout Week 9 prep as he dealt with a back injury. The kick returner and No. 4 wide receiver for the Rams is all set to suit up for Sunday's game as he looks to play through the issue.

items.headline: Williams carried the ball 15 times for 45 yards and caught three of four targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 20-13 win over Washington.
items.summary: Blake Corum was the more productive Ram on the ground, turning 11 carries into 58 yards and a touchdown, but the offense mainly flowed through Puka Nacua on the afternoon. Williams failed to find the end zone for only the third time in nine games this season, and the 45 rushing yards were his lowest total since Week 1, although he has yet to reach 100 in any contest. The Los Angeles backfield has become a clear timeshare however, limiting Williams' upside heading into a Week 10 trip to Arizona.

items.headline: Head coach Sean McVay said Wednesday that Adams had successful surgery on his left hamstring, and the Rams are hopeful that the wide receiver will be able to return on the early side of his 6-to-10-week recovery timetable, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
items.summary: Adams tweaked his hamstring on the Rams' final offensive possession of a Week 6 loss to the Cardinals on Oct. 18, and McVay revealed one day later that the wide receiver had a rupture of the hamstring and required surgery, with the aim to return "a little after" the Rams' Week 11 bye. L.A. seems to be targeting a Week 12 matchup with the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25, which is a shade more than six weeks from the initial injury. In any case, Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington and Tutu Atwell will continue to earn the WR reps behind top option Puka Nacua.

items.headline: Connors (hand) was placed on IR on Tuesday, Blaine Grisak of SI.com reports.
items.summary: Connors broke his hand in Sunday's win over the Chargers and is slated for surgery. He's worked as a core special-teamer this season but hasn't logged a snap on offense. As such, Connors' IR stint -- which will last at least four games -- isn't likely to cause any waves in fantasy.

items.headline: Allen is listed as active for Sunday's matchup against the Lions.
items.summary: Allen is officially active for Sunday's matchup against the Lions after finishing the week with full participation in practice Friday. The 23-year-old plays had been playing a majority of his snaps on special teams, but with Jaylen Wright (quad) inactive versus Detroit, Allen and Carlos Washington are the backs who would be in line pick up extra Week 9 carries if top RB Ollie Gordon were to leave the game for any reason.

items.headline: Bell caught three of his four targets for 25 yards in the Dolphins' 28-25 win over the Jets on Sunday.
items.summary: The third-round rookie played 31 offensive snaps and five special-teams snaps in the contest. Bell was in on 48 percent of the Dolphins' offensive plays and saw the second-most targets behind tight end Greg Dulcich (five).

items.headline: Coleman caught all three of his targets for 46 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 24-19 loss to the Patriots.
items.summary: Coleman led the team in receiving yards while reeling in multiple passes for the second time this season. The wide receiver's biggest moment of the game came in the fourth quarter when he connected with quarterback Malik Willis for a 35-yard score with 2:04 remaining in regulation. Coleman hasn't been a consistent part of the team's offensive approach this season, catching eight of 21 targets for 82 yards and two scores over seven contests so far.

items.headline: Gordon rushed 16 times for 55 yards and brought in his only target for nine yards in the Dolphins' 19-9 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
items.summary: Gordon worked in the lead role as expected but found running room at a premium against a game Lions defense. Gordon has at least Sunday's carry total in four straight games, but he's now seen his rushing yardage total decline in consecutive games. Jaylen Wright's inactive status due to a quadriceps injury helped Gordon's touch floor overall, and the latter should remain the top option in Miami's ground attack in a favorable Week 10 road matchup against the Colts next Sunday.

items.headline: Kacmarek is dealing with a quad injury and is questionable to return to Sunday's clash against Detroit.
items.summary: Kacmarek took a low hit after making a catch in the third quarter and subsequently went to the medical tent. He then returned to the sideline and tested out the injured leg, so he appears to be at least attempting to re-enter the contest. If Kacmarek can't return, however, Greg Dulcich and Seydou Traore will be Miami's two healthy active tight ends.

items.headline: Miami elevated Washington from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday ahead of Sunday's tilt against Detroit.
items.summary: Washington's elevation is his second of the campaign. He was active for Week 5 and logged nine offensive snaps, along with three special-teams snaps, against Cincinnati, but he finished without any touches or targets. His workload against the Lions will likely depend on whether Jaylen Wright and Kaytron Allen, both of whom are questionable due to quad injuries, are able to suit up.

items.headline: Wayne (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game versus the Patriots.
items.summary: Wayne was limited in Wednesday and Thursday's practice sessions. He was a full participant Friday and didn't carry an injury designation for the Week 8 meeting with New England. However, despite being healthy enough to suit up, the wideout won't be on the field Sunday.

items.headline: Wright (quadriceps) is listed as inactive Sunday against the Lions.
items.summary: After sitting out Wednesday's practice due to a quadriceps injury, Wright was able to get back to limited Thursday and maintain that activity level Friday, at which point he was tagged as questionable in advance of the weekend. On Sunday morning, however, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported that Wright wasn't expected to suit up, and that's now locked in. With Wright out of the lineup, Kaytron Allen (quad) and Carlos Washington will serve as the reserve RB options behind Ollie Gordon.

items.headline: Source: Browns returning to Watson as QB1 despite Sanders' strong fill-in start
items.summary: The Browns plan to start Deshaun Watson in Week 10 against the Texans, a source told ESPN's Jeremy Fowler on Monday.

items.headline: Addison caught three of eight targets for 66 yards in Sunday's 19-15 loss to the Lions.
items.summary: Addison's big play was a 51-yard catch over the top of the defense in the fourth quarter to set the offense up at the 10-yard line. T.J. Hockenson scored a go-ahead touchdown two plays later. Addison's eight targets on the day were one fewer than Justin Jefferson, but it was the former who paced the team in receiving yards. Playing in a Minnesota offense that doesn't push the ball down the field much or focus on its outside receivers, Addison has just 16 catches for 249 yards and one touchdown on 33 targets through six games this season. He'll be a fantasy WR4 with upside next Monday night against a leaky Bills secondary.

items.headline: The Vikings are signing Beckham from the practice squad to the active roster, Tom Pelissero of NFL Network reports.
items.summary: Beckham kicked off the season with the Giants but was targeted just one time through the first three contests before the team released him Sept. 29. He then joined the Vikings on the practice squad and was elevated for Week 5 but eventually was inactive. Thus, if Beckham is able to avoid such a listing Monday against the Bills, it'll mark the sixth different organization in which he's suited up in his career.

items.headline: Brosmer is set to back up Carson Wentz against the Bills on Monday, as Kyler Murray (hamstring) won't play, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: It would likely take an injury to Wentz for Brosmer to get into the game, but the latter moves one step closer to getting on the field for the first time in 2026. Brosmer didn't look like an NFL-caliber QB as a rookie in 2025, posting a 0:4 TD:INT across seven appearances, including two starts.

items.headline: Claiborne (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's battle against Buffalo, Craig Peters of the Vikings' official site reports.
items.summary: Claiborne didn't practice Friday or Saturday after suffering a knee injury in practice Wednesday. Head coach Kevin O'Connell said he doesn't think Claiborne will need surgery but added that the team is still evaluating the injury. The running back has played sparingly this season, logging 18 offensive snaps through four games and tallying 13 yards on six carries along with eight yards on two receptions.

items.headline: Dallas was signed to the Vikings' active roster Wednesday, Craig Peters of the team's official website reports.
items.summary: Dallas will return to the active roster after playing in the first five contests of the year with the Vikings before being released and ultimately returning to the team as a member of the practice squad in late October. The running back has rushed four times for 14 yards and caught all four of his targets for 34 yards over seven contests with Minnesota this year, and he figures to operate in an extreme depth role behind Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason on Monday night versus Buffalo.

items.headline: Hockenson caught four of five targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 19-15 loss to the Lions.
items.summary: Hockenson secured an eight-yard touchdown midway through the fourth quarter to give the Vikings a 15-12 lead, and he's now up to 31 grabs for 295 yards and three touchdowns on 37 targets through seven games this season. Hockenson, though, missed all but two offensive snaps in the Week 5 win over the Saints after suffering a concussion. A favorite target for Kyler Murray in the middle and short areas of the field, Hockenson has settled in as a lower-end TE1 in fantasy. He gets a plus matchup with the Bills next Monday night in another spot the Minnesota offense may be forced to push the gas pedal.

items.headline: Mason rushed eight times for 20 yards in the Vikings' 19-15 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
items.summary: Playing in his second game since returning from an IR stint due to a thumb injury, Mason paced the Vikings' ground attack in carries but finished two yards behind Aaron Jones, who logged five totes. Mason also wasn't targeted for the second time in three games, and Minnesota's running game figures to continue in a fantasy-averse timeshare between the two. Mason will look to make inroads against what has been an improved Bills run defense in a Week 9 home showdown on Monday night, Nov. 9.

items.headline: The Vikings placed Briscoe (undisclosed) on their practice squad injured list Wednesday.
items.summary: It's not immediately clear exactly what happened, but as a result of the move, Briscoe will not be eligible for elevation to the active roster for Minnesota's next four games. He's still waiting to make his regular-season debut since entering the league as an undrafted free agent in May.

items.headline: Minnesota signed Culp to its practice squad Wednesday.
items.summary: Just a little more than a week after getting cut from the Browns' practice squad, Culp has now found another opportunity with a new club. He suited up for 13 games with the Buccaneers in 2025, catching his only target for six yards and a touchdown.

items.headline: Douglas brought in five of nine targets for 102 yards in the Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Packers on Sunday.
items.summary: Douglas tied for the team lead in receptions and set the pace in both receiving yards and targets while serving as Drake Maye's top target in the absence of A.J. Brown (knee) and Romeo Doubs (IR, shoulder). Douglas also recorded a team-high 36-yard grab among his five catches, and both the yardage and target tallies were season highs. Douglas has at least 76 receiving yards in three of the past four games heading into a Week 10 matchup against the Lions in Germany next Sunday.

items.headline: Hollins caught three of six targets for 36 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Patriots.
items.summary: After missing four weeks on injured reserve with a calf injury, Hollins returned to the lineup Sunday and immediately became a central part of the offense, tying Kyle Williams for second on the team with 34 routes on 46 dropbacks by New England's quarterbacks. Hollins' six targets also tied Eli Raridon for second on the team behind DeMario Douglas' nine. With A.J. Brown (knee) and Romeo Doubs (shoulder) still not 100 percent, Hollins figures to remain a big part of the picture next Sunday against the Lions in a potential shootout under the dome at Ford Field.

items.headline: Kiner rushed eight times for 55 yards and a touchdown and returned nine kickoffs for 224 yards in the Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Packers on Sunday.
items.summary: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) was inactive and Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) exited the game in the second half, a pair of developments that, when paired with the blowout nature of the contest, afforded Kiner some solid run. The Cincinnati product eclipsed the 50-yard mark on the ground for the third time this season, and he finished as the team leader in rushing yards. Kiner also recorded his first career touchdown on a four-yard run with just under four minutes remaining, and he'll be in line for an expanded role in Week 10 against the Lions in Germany if neither Stevenson nor Henderson are available.

items.headline: The Patriots signed Larison off the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: The addition of Larison to the 53-man roster gives the Patriots more depth in the backfield, and he could see some offensive snaps against the Dolphins on Sunday due to the absence of TreVeyon Henderson (illness). Larison figures to operate as the RB3 behind Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner.

items.headline: Morton (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Patriots' emergency third quarterback against the Packers on Sunday.
items.summary: As the emergency third quarterback, Morton is not allowed to play Sunday unless both Drake Maye and Tommy DeVito are removed from the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Raridon had one reception for five yards on four targets in New England's 24-19 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
items.summary: Raridon's lone reception went for five yards early in the first quarter. He didn't record another catch for the remainder of the contest despite logging a hefty 93 percent offensive snap share, largely due to No .1 tight end Hunter Henry departing in the first half due to a foot injury. Should Henry remain sidelined in Week 9, Raridon will have another big opportunity to produce in a home tilt against Green Bay.

items.headline: Williams caught his lone target for a 43-yard touchdown during Sunday's 24-19 win over the Dolphins.
items.summary: Williams made the most of his only touch in Week 8, scoring on a 43-yard deep ball from Drake Maye in the third quarter. The wide receiver had an opportunity to be more involved with A.J. Brown (knee) sidelined Sunday, but Williams saw just one target for the third game in a row. On the year, the wide receiver has now caught seven of 13 targets for 190 yards and two touchdowns over eight regular-season contests.

items.headline: New England signed Jennings to its practice squad Monday.
items.summary: Jennings is a familiar face for the Patriots, as he suited up for 10 regular-season games with them over the last two campaigns, taking 36 carries for 106 yards and a touchdown. With 2025 second-rounder TreVeyon Henderson dealing with an illness that sidelined him in Week 8, New England is understandably looking to add some organizational depth in its backfield.

items.headline: Miller reverted to the Patriots' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's official transaction log.
items.summary: The wide receiver was elevated for New England's Week 8 win over Miami after the team ruled out A.J. Brown (knee/ankle). Miller saw action on five offensive snaps but did not record a catch. Brown's status next week could go a long way toward determining whether Miller is elevated again.

items.headline: Brown hauled in all three targets for 57 yards during Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Steelers.
items.summary: Brown had the most productive game of his NFL career thus far, catching more passes than he had in his previous five appearances combined. The 2026 No. 190 overall pick should continue to get consistent work on special teams. However, despite the recent uptick in offensive snaps, it's unknown if Brown will continue to be more involved as a pass catcher moving forward.

items.headline: Donaldson (shoulder/concussion) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Browns, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
items.summary: With Donaldson out and Travis Etienne (hamstring) still on injured reserve, the Saints will roll with a three-man backfield of Alvin Kamara, Kendre Miller and Audric Estime. One of the league's least productive backfields doesn't evoke much fantasy excitement.

items.headline: Fant gathered in all two targets for 11 yards during Sunday's 16-10 defeat against Pittsburgh.
items.summary: After finding the end zone twice in the loss to the Raiders in Week 3, Fant has combined for just three catches in his previous three appearances. While his two receptions Sunday were a small step in the right direction, he is expected to continue to play second fiddle to Juwan Johnson moving forward. It may also be a matter of time before rookie Oscar Delp logs more snaps from week to week.

items.headline: Kamara rushed six times for 32 yards while catching three of four targets for 17 yards during Sunday's 23-22 overtime win against the Browns.
items.summary: Kamara operated as the team's No. 2 option in the backfield behind Audric Estime (15-72-1) in Week 9. Estime was claimed off waivers from the Browns on Tuesday, and he immediately supplanted Kamara as the team's lead back. Kamara has yet to exceed 40 rushing yards in a game this season, and he has scored just one touchdown over the team's last four contests combined.

items.headline: Lance reeled in all two targets for 12 yards during Sunday's 16-10 loss to Pittsburgh.
items.summary: Lance had two catches for the second consecutive game, though unlike the Week 6 win over the Giants, he didn't find the end zone. The 24-year-old has logged 332 offensive snaps this season, third in the receiving corps behind Chris Olave (387) and Devaughn Vele (438). However, despite being on the field more often than most of the other wideouts on the roster, Lance hasn't been productive thus far in his rookie campaign.

items.headline: Olave caught seven of 12 targets for 98 yards in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over Cleveland.
items.summary: The fifth-year wideout led the Saints in catches, targets and receiving yards once again, but Juwan Johnson was on the other end of Tyler Shough's only TD of the day. Olave is the clear top option in the New Orleans passing attack, but with Jordyn Tyson finally making his pro debut Sunday, secondaries may have someone else to worry about in the second half of the season. Olave will take a 56-734-2 line on 83 targets into a Week 10 battle against the Panthers.

items.headline: Tillman reverted to the Saints' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's official transaction log.
items.summary: Tillman was elevated to the active roster for the third week in a row before Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Steelers in Paris. The wide receiver didn't log any stats while playing one snap on offense and five snaps with the special-teams unit. Tillman will now have to be officially signed to the active roster in order to play in another contest with New Orleans this season.

items.headline: The Saints elevated White from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday ahead of Sunday's matchup against Cleveland.
items.summary: White has been on New Orleans' practice squad all season, waiting for a gameday opportunity. He'll get that chance Sunday after Kendre Miller was waived Saturday and CJ Donaldson (shoulder/concussion) was ruled out from facing the Browns. With that said, White may not get an extensive look, as Alvin Kamara and possibly Audric Estime are ahead of him on the RB depth chart.

items.headline: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Saints' emergency third quarterback against the Browns on Sunday.
items.summary: The former Jet remains the odd-quarterback out for the Saints. Wilson will not be allowed to play in Sunday's contest unless both Tyler Shough and Spencer Rattler leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Head coach Kellen Moore said Wednesday that the Saints haven't opened Etienne's (hamstring) practice window just yet, Jeff Nowak of WWL Louisiana reports.
items.summary: Etienne has missed the required four games on IR due to a strained left hamstring, but even with the benefit of a Week 8 bye, he hasn't gained clearance to mix into drills. Moore told Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana on Monday that Etienne has a chance to return to practice this week, but with no on-field work to begin Week 9 prep, he seems to be on the outside looking in to have enough time to be activated for Sunday's contest against the Browns.

items.headline: Desrosiers could serve as a backup for the Giants on Sunday, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Desrosiers is listed as running back No. 3 on the Giants' depth chart and could be in line to back up Devin Singletary on Sunday if Cam Skattebo can't play after being listed as questionable with a hamstring injury. Desrosiers has yet to play in a regular-season game this season. In three preseason games, he rushed 23 times for 166 yards and a touchdown.

items.headline: Fidone (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's contest in Philadelphia, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
items.summary: Fidone suited up for each of New York's previous three games before a Week 8 bye, but he's a healthy scratch against the Eagles. The second-year tight end has worked mostly on special teams this season and has one catch for 29 yards on one target over three contests. Fidone figures to be at risk for inactive status when the three tight ends ahead of him in the pecking order -- Isaiah Likely, Theo Johnson and Chris Manhertz -- are healthy.

items.headline: The Giants signed Hyatt from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Hyatt was a regular part of the wideout corps with New York during his first two NFL seasons, but his role was reduced dramatically last year, and he's spent most of 2026 on the team's practice squad. He saw his first regular-season action as a practice-squad elevation in Week 7 versus Houston and played 10 total snaps (four on offense and six on special teams) without otherwise getting into the box score. Hyatt doesn't figure to see much work on offense Sunday against Philadelphia, though he could receive a slight bump if Charlie Jones (who is questionable due to a hand injury) can't suit up.

items.headline: Johnson (neck) was a full participant at the Giants' practice Wednesday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Johnson appears to be back to full health after missing the team's last two contests while nursing a neck injury. The 25-year-old will be back in his No. 2 role at tight end behind starter Isaiah Likely against the Eagles on Sunday.

items.headline: Jones (hand) is active for Sunday's game against the Eagles, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Jones was limited throughout Week 9 prep with a thumb injury. The wide receiver is not only active but was not wearing a cast or brace over the injured appendage as he fielded punts in pregame warmups.

items.headline: The Giants elevated Mafah from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Mafah joined New York's practice squad in mid-September, and he'll get his first chance with the club's gameday roster Sunday versus the Eagles. The Clemson product played in one game as a rookie with Dallas last season, garnering 18 yards and a touchdown on five carries along with two catches for 11 yards on two targets in Week 18. Cam Skattebo (hamstring) is doubtful to suit up Sunday, so Mafah could work in tandem with Greg Desrosiers behind Devin Singletary.

items.headline: Mooney caught one of three targets for four yards and rushed once for three yards during Sunday's 27-21 overtime win against the Texans.
items.summary: Mooney has now been held to one or no catches in three of the past four games, and he has yet to exceed two receptions in a contest this season. The wide receiver will continue to be an unattractive fantasy option when the Giants return to action Week 9 against the Eagles.

items.headline: Winston turned four carries into four yards and a touchdown during the Giants' 27-21 overtime win over the Texans on Sunday.
items.summary: The Giants turned to J.J. McCarthy to serve as the starting quarterback for Week 7 after Winston filled in that role in each of the four prior games. McCarthy looked more poised in the pocket, but all four of the Giants' touchdowns came on the ground, with Winston finding the end zone on a designed QB sneak late in the second quarter. That figures to be the veteran's role moving forward unless McCarthy misses time.

items.headline: The Giants cut Brownlee from the practice squad Tuesday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
items.summary: Brownlee has appeared in 13 regular-season games for the Jets and Chiefs during his career, catching five passes (nine targets) for 56 yards and one touchdown. The 27-year-old has experience, so he could get an opportunity elsewhere, though it may be as a member of another team's practice squad.

items.headline: The Giants signed Gray to their practice squad Monday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
items.summary: Gray is back with the organization that drafted him back in 2023 after spending some time early in the season on the Browns' practice squad. With Cam Skattebo dealing with a hamstring issue, there's a chance Gray could end up being elevated to the active roster for the Giants' contest at Philadelphia in Week 9.

items.headline: The Giants signed Haener to their practice squad Saturday,Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Haener has been part of New York's active roster twice this season, and he was most recently waived by the team Thursday. The Fresno State product will remain in the organization on the practice squad, as the Giants have J.J. McCarthy and Jameis Winston as their quarterbacks on game days. Should one of those two get injured and need to miss time, Haener figures to be elevated or signed to the roster again.

items.headline: Davis rushed five times for 15 yards in Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders.
items.summary: With Breece Hall (quad) missing another game, Davis handled RB2 duties behind workhorse Braelon Allen. Davis has totaled 15 carries for 44 empty yards this season, adding five catches for 68 yards. Hall is expected to return for Week 9 against the Chiefs, which would relegate Davis to the RB3 role.

items.headline: Mitchell failed to reel in any of his seven targets during Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.
items.summary: Mitchell finished second on the team in targets behind fellow wideout Omar Cooper (11) with Garrett Wilson (concussion) unavailable. Mitchell has now gone without a reception in two of the last three contests, but he has garnered 19 targets in the last three weeks, and he figures to remain busy in Week 10 against the Bills.

items.headline: Nwangwu was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
items.summary: Nwangwu remained inactive for the Jets' Week 7 loss to the Dolphins despite logging a full practice Friday. The running back has returned to form for Week 8 prep and should be all set to suit up for Sunday's game against the Raiders.

items.headline: Sadiq caught all four of his targets for 49 yards in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.
items.summary: After taking a back seat to Mason Taylor in recent weeks, Sadiq out-targeted his tight end teammate four to two against Kansas City. The rookie also closed the gap on Taylor in terms of routes, as Taylor ran 21 to Sadiq's 20 on Geno Smith's 38 dropbacks. It was easily Sadiq's most productive game since posting a 7-105-1 line in Week 3 against Detroit. He's not yet playable in most fantasy formats.

items.headline: Taylor (back) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
items.summary: Taylor was limited Wednesday, but his return to full Thursday puts him on track for his normal role Sunday against the Chiefs. The tight end has been a surprisingly big part of the passing offense this season despite the selection of Kenyon Sadiq in the first round of April's Draft. Taylor has secured 17 of 23 targets for 136 yards and two touchdowns across six games.

items.headline: Williams caught an 18-yard touchdown on his lone target in Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders.
items.summary: Williams ran a total of one route on Geno Smith's 35 dropbacks against Las Vegas, but he made it count with a red-zone touchdown. The Jets' fourth receiver behind Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper, Williams has no fantasy appeal headed into next Sunday's date with the Chiefs.

items.headline: Patrick is inactive (coach's decision) for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
items.summary: Garrett Wilson is sitting out due to a concussion, but Patrick still won't suit up for Sunday's contest. The 32-year-old has been a healthy scratch the past two weeks after catching three passes for 41 yards in the previous three games.

items.headline: The Jets signed Manjack to the practice squad Wednesday, Amanda Vogt of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: The undrafted rookie receiver out of TCU had previously spent time with Denver in the offseason, appearing in all three preseason games while catching three of four targets for 40 yards.
